title: Pramukh Villa
tagline: A serene sanctuary of raw concrete, rustic brick, and nature.
summary: Pramukh Villa explores the honest interplay between raw materiality and verdant nature. Designed for quiet luxury living in Atladra, the residence synthesizes exposed brickwork, tactile concrete textures, and lush courtyards into a harmonious, light-filled domestic retreat.
overview: Located in Atladra, Vadodara, Pramukh Villa reinterprets contemporary suburban living by embedding nature into the very spine of the home. The design celebrates tactile materials—rustic brick, exposed concrete finishes, and handcrafted timber elements—fostering an atmosphere of calm permanence. Sunlight filters through customized fluted glass and deep openings, bathing internal courtyards and open living volumes in dynamic daylight throughout the day.
concept: The design concept was guided by three principles: architectural honesty, indoor-outdoor connectivity, and quiet material dignity. Rather than isolating greenery as an ornamental afterthought, landscaping is woven directly into interior corners and transitional thresholds.
keyFeatures: Seamless visual and physical flow between the living areas and perimeter green pockets
Tactile palette of rustic masonry, exposed concrete formwork, and rich teak accents
Custom fluted glass partitions balancing spatial privacy with diffused natural light
Climatically responsive overhangs mitigating western glare while maximizing cross ventilation

credits.principals: Shivali Agrawal, Kunal Patel, Azaz Saleh

title: Vairaag
tagline: Modern-rustic suburban villa framing light through corten steel artistry.
summary: Named as an affectionate portmanteau of homeowners Vaishali and Gaurang, Vairaag merges modern-rustic sensibilities with raw concrete, exposed brick, and bespoke corten steel jalis that cast intricate shadow poetry into peaceful living spaces.
overview: Set along Bill Road in suburban Vadodara, Vairaag stands as a testament to contextual luxury. The villa's envelope presents an expressive conversation between brutalist board-formed concrete, earthen brickwork, and warm corten steel latticework. Within, the home unfolds as a fluid sanctuary of warm textured Oikos walls, custom sculptural lighting, and artisanal Indian craft elements curated for modern domestic life.
concept: The concept originated from the clients' desire for a grounding residence that felt deeply personal and timeless. The architects conceptualized the dwelling as an acoustic and thermal refuge, using customized metal screens (jalis) to temper intense sunlight while animating internal floors with geometric patterns of light and shadow.
keyFeatures: Custom laser-cut Corten steel jali screens providing privacy and dynamic daylight casting
Handcrafted exposed brick masonry laid in textured courses alongside raw concrete surfaces
Textured Oikos Italian wall finishes paired with bespoke brass-inlaid teak furnishings
Seamless indoor-verandah transition orienting living spaces toward private landscaped gardens

credits.principals: Shivali Agrawal, Kunal Patel, Azaz Saleh
credits.published: Volume Zero (Hot 100 Selection) & The Architect's Diary

title: Shayonam
tagline: An artful nucleus of modern architecture and ethnic design heritage.
summary: Spanning four dramatic levels and nearly 10,000 square feet, Shayonam is a tour-de-force of contemporary Indian residential luxury. It masterfully bridges expansive double-height volumes with intricate ethnic woodwork, CNC-crafted motifs, and tactile materiality.
overview: Published in The Architect's Diary as an 'artful nucleus of modern and ethnic design body,' Shayonam is designed to accommodate multi-generational living with effortless grace. Organized across four interconnected levels, the home features grand public entertaining halls, intimate private suites, dedicated wellness zones, and serene prayer spaces. The material vocabulary brings together raw exposed concrete, rich warm teak, fluted paneling, and delicate brass accents.
concept: The spatial narrative balances traditional Indian joint-family cultural values with international contemporary living standards. Every level is connected through a vertical atrium bathed in natural overhead daylight, creating visual connections across floors while maintaining acoustic comfort and thermal zoning.
keyFeatures: Monumental 4-level spatial arrangement spanning 9,795 square feet of bespoke built space
Skylit central stair atrium creating dynamic vertical dialogue and continuous illumination
Artisan CNC-milled wooden screens and ethnic ceiling motifs harmonized with sleek modern profiles
Luxurious master suites with integrated dressing lounges and spa-inspired natural stone ensuites

credits.principals: Shivali Agrawal, Kunal Patel, Azaz Saleh

title: Isha Developers Office
tagline: Permanent site office redefining workplace through exposed brick, concrete, and green courtyards.
summary: Breaking away from the temporary, utilitarian nature of typical property site offices, Isha Developers Office is a permanent, climatically responsive architectural statement of exposed concrete, brick motifs, sloping roofs, and an open courtyard core.
overview: Designed for a forward-thinking real estate development firm in Vadodara, this 1,500 sq. ft. office faces the main road with commanding quiet presence. Foresight Associates departed from modular site containers to craft a permanent, tactile pavilion. Featuring sloping terracotta roof profiles, broad granite plinths, exposed Kota stone floors, and a central open-to-sky planter courtyard, the structure warmly welcomes prospective buyers and team members alike.
concept: The concept reinterprets the traditional Indian chowk (central courtyard). By anchoring the plan around a central green courtyard covered by an overhead cast-iron jali, daylight penetrates deep into administrative workspaces while filtering thermal gain.
keyFeatures: Permanent architectural character breaking free of generic prefabricated site offices
Central micro-courtyard core with lush ficus planter and natural Kota stone paving
Overhead cast-iron jali canopy casting intricate shadow silhouettes across raw brick masonry
Sloping roof volume paired with full-height glazing for panoramic sightlines into surroundings

credits.principals: Shivali Agrawal, Kunal Patel, Azaz Saleh
